threads.title: Personal Guide To Writing Lorebooks For Spicychat Ai

messages.author: Duke
messages.content:
*Based on my experience using lorebooks on SpicyChat, here’s what I’ve found works best for creating consistent, usable, and effective lore for world-building and storytelling.*

**How Lorebooks Work**

Lorebooks are structured guides that help the AI remember context, maintain consistency, and respond according to your world or story. They are not meant to replace character creation.

*Keyword Triggers:* Specific words or phrases that, when mentioned in chat, prompt the AI to reference relevant lore entries.

*Memory Reinforcement:* Keeps characters, settings, and story elements consistent across interactions.

World-Building: Ideal for RPGs, fanfiction, or interactive storytelling where internal logic and continuity matter.

From my personal experience, thinking of a lorebook as a tool to guide the AI, rather than a book or character itself, gives the best results.

messages.author: Duke
messages.content:
**How Keywords Work**

Keywords activate whenever they appear in chat, typed by you or the AI.

They stay active for about two turns (your message + the AI’s response) and extend if the keyword keeps appearing.

To prevent over-triggering, choose specific phrases instead of broad terms.

Example:
✅ “Expedition to Ocean”
❌ “trip”, “beach”, “sea”

messages.author: Duke
messages.content:
**Best Practices from My Experience**

*Keep Entries Short and Precise*

The AI only loads a portion of the lore at once (around 20% of context memory).

Long, dense entries may be ignored—short, focused entries work best.

Use Clear, Descriptive Titles

Example: Instead of “Magic”, use “Mana Crystal Types” or “Forbidden Rituals of Eclipsara”.

Organize by Category

Locations, Factions, Items, Mechanics, Rules, Events.

Helps keep your lorebook navigable and structured.

Include Keyword Variants

Synonyms, alternate spellings, and nicknames prevent the AI from missing entries.

Example: “Qi Crystal”, “Qi Crystals”, “Qi Stone”.

Leverage Placeholders

{char}, {user}, {npc} make entries reusable across multiple characters.

Example: “{char} carries a unique Qi Crystal that glows in moonlight.”

Avoid Over-Triggers

Broad keywords activate too often. Compound phrases work better.

Example: “Ancient Moon Ritual” instead of just “Moon”.

Test and Adjust

Test your lorebook in conversation to see if keywords trigger correctly.

Adjust keywords, split long entries, or rewrite context as needed.

Meta Notes (Optional)

Include guidance for AI behavior.

Example: “When discussing politics, maintain character neutrality unless prompted otherwise.”

messages.author: Duke
messages.content:
What Lorebooks Are Not

One common mistake: trying to make full characters in a lorebook. From my experience:

**Lorebooks are for world-building, not character sheets.**

Example: Instead of a lorebook about a single Hazbin Hotel character, create a lorebook about the setting—its city, factions, rules, and events. This allows multiple characters to interact naturally within the same world.

messages.author: Duke
messages.content:
**Summary of Best Practices**

*Think of a lorebook as a guide for the AI, not a character.*

*Keep entries short, precise, and context-focused.*

*Use specific keywords and variants.*

*Organize by category for easy navigation.*

*Test your lorebook to ensure proper keyword activation.*

*Optional: include meta notes to guide AI behavior.*

Following these practices has been the most effective way I’ve found to use lorebooks on SpicyChat keeping world-building consistent, conversations smooth, and stories immersive.

messages.author: Nomn07
messages.content:
Can Lorebooks keep more than one entry open? 
Or when one is opened, does the other close? 
What happens if I activate two entries at the same time in a sentence? 
Like: "The Scepter of the Undead King" and "War Against the Abyss" Are both entries activated?

messages.author: Jayjayxjay
messages.content: It can hold multiple entries open, up to 20% of the total context memory.

messages.author: Duke
messages.content: if the same keyword is triggered it will load those memory into context in order until the context is filled the extra tokens will be pushed out of context, meaning yes it will but extra information in the other entries will not be fully used
